attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as a one-armed load balancer: TCP port 80 on its LAN/management address (10.100.6.10) round-robins to node2 and node3's HTTP servers on port 8080 via a pf rdr-to pool rule plus a matching outbound SNAT rule that masquerades traffic to the backends as coming from node1 (required because backend replies otherwise bypassed NAT translation and returned directly to the client — an asymmetric routing issue). Verified node4 receives alternating responses identifying node2 and node3 through the single port-80 entry point. Also disabled OPNsense's automatic HTTP->HTTPS webgui redirect (disablehttpredirect) since it owned port 80 via an anti-lockout no-rdr rule that shadowed the new DNAT rule. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with captured baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery verification for each.
